artifacts.summary: Research on adding an independently-gated orphaned Lean LSP process-tree reclamation pass to claude-refresh.sh, grounded in live process inspection and leanclient/lean_lsp_mcp source.

memory_candidates.content: On Linux, ps's `comm` field for lean-lsp-mcp's spawned processes is just `lake` or `lean` -- it never renders the full argv (`lake serve`, `lean --server`, `lean --worker`). Distinguishing these three requires an args-substring match in addition to the comm gate, the same two-part pattern claude-refresh.sh's is_claude_executable_comm already uses for its `node` branch (comm gate + argv pattern gate). Also: `ps -eo ... -C <name>` silently ignores the -C filter and returns the whole process table; `ps -C <name> -o ...` (without -e) is the correct filtered form.

lake serve / lean --server retain a controlling TTY inherited from the pty of whatever spawned them (e.g. lean-lsp-mcp), even when the owning session is fully gone -- only lean --worker children show tty=='?'. Any orphan-detection heuristic keyed on tty=='?' as a necessary signal will miss an orphaned lake serve/lean --server pair; a process-family-specific detection pass needs its own candidacy predicate independent of TTY.

leanclient's BaseLeanLSPClient spawns `subprocess.Popen(["lake", "serve", "--", "-Dserver.reportDelayMs=0"], ...)` (base_client.py) and lean_lsp_mcp's client_utils.py only tears clients down via _close_client() at explicit eviction/restart-failure/shutdown -- there is no idle-timeout or LRU-by-inactivity mechanism in the installed package, so a spawned lake serve -> lean --server -> lean --worker* tree lives as long as the MCP host process does unless something external reclaims it.
